claims.claim: **Alkalis include** drain and oven cleaners, automatic dishwashing liquids and powders, laundry detergents, ammonia and Portland cement.
claims.source_text: Alkalis include: Drain cleaners, Oven cleaners Automatic dish washing liquids & powders Laundry detergents, Ammonia Portland cement
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **pH over 11.5 is likely to cause significant GI ulceration.**
claims.source_text: pH of >11.5 is likely to cause significant GI ulceration
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Get the container** to check contents and strength. Corrosive potential varies with concentration and preparation: **liquids are more likely than powders to burn the oesophagus.**
claims.source_text: Attempt to obtain container to check contents and strength of substance. … Corrosive potential varies with concentration of specific ingredients and preparations, ie liquid preparations are more likely to cause oesophageal burns than powders.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check the product with the Poisons Information Centre** to establish whether it is weak, strong, irritant or corrosive.
claims.source_text: Check preparations with Poisons Information Centre to determine whether ingested substance is weak, strong, irritant or corrosive in nature.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Exposure can severely burn the GI tract, especially the oesophagus.** **No mouth or pharyngeal ulcers does not rule out gastro-oesophageal lesions.**
claims.source_text: Exposure may lead to severe burns of GIT, especially oesophagus Absence of mouth or pharyngeal ulcers does not preclude gastro-oesophageal lesions
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptoms may be minimal:** pain · nausea and vomiting · drooling or refusing to eat and drink · ⚠️ stridor or respiratory distress.
claims.source_text: Symptoms: May be minimal Pain Nausea & vomiting, drooling or refusing to eat and drink Stridor, respiratory distress
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic: fluid dilution with water 10 mL/kg, max 250 mL.**
claims.source_text: If asymptomatic treat with fluid dilution: 10 ml/kg of water (max 250 ml)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** if still asymptomatic after 4 hours and able to eat and drink.
claims.source_text: If asymptomatic after 4 hours and able to eat and drink the patient can be safely discharged
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any symptoms: contact the surgical registrar and admit for oesophagoscopy.**
claims.source_text: If any symptoms, contact surgical registrar, & admit for oesophagoscopy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
